title: A Kidney Transplant, Ignored Advice, and a President’s Surprise Pick to Run a $160 Billion Pacific Island Mine
content:
Almost 40 years after it descended into a devastating civil war, the autonomous region of Bougainville is on the cusp of achieving independence from Papua New Guinea. At its heart sits Panguna, a long-shuttered gold and copper mine worth an estimated $160 billion.

To relaunch the Panguna mine and generate the type of economic development that could support the impoverished region’s bid for full sovereignty, Bougainville’s majority state-owned mining company spent around 10 months on a public search for an international partner, speaking to some of the world’s largest and most experienced mining companies.

But last November, Bougainville President Ishmael Toroama made a shock announcement: he had signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to redevelop the mine with Lloyds Metals and Energy Ltd, a publicly-traded Indian company with no background in major copper and gold extraction.

The long-shuttered Panguna mine, estimated to contain up to $160 billion worth of copper and gold, as seen on May 21, 2026. (Credit: Michael E. Miller/OCCRP)

title: Armenia Detains Ex-President Kocharyan in Corruption Probe
content:
Armenian authorities detained former President Robert Kocharyan and his son Sedrak on Tuesday as part of a corruption investigation into the alleged acquisition of state property at below-market prices. The country’s Anti-Corruption Committee said six people had been detained and alleged that the former president and people close to him used his official position to remove valuable assets from the state, acquire them at significantly reduced prices and subsequently conceal their ownership through affiliated companies. 

Kocharyan’s office called the operation another “attack by the authorities against President Kocharyan and his family.” 

The former president has previously rejected corruption allegations against him as politically motivated. OCCRP reported in 2019 that Kocharyan had been accused of accepting bribes while in office; his lawyer told OCCRP at the time that the allegations were fabricated. A court found there was insufficient evidence to support the corruption allegation at the level of reasonable suspicion.

title: Kazakhstan’s Election Brings a New Parliament — and More Pressure on Journalists
content:
Kazakhstan’s first election to a new unicameral Parliament on Sunday gave a commanding victory to the newly formed, pro-presidential Adilet, or “Justice,” party, in a vote that press-freedom advocates said was held amid mounting pressure on independent journalists.

Adilet won 71.17 percent of the vote, or about 6.5 million ballots, while turnout was 74 percent, according to results released Tuesday by Kazakhstan’s Central Election Commission. Four other parties cleared the five-percent threshold.

None of the seven parties that took part in the election could be seen as opposing President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev’s policies, according to international observers.

The new 145-seat legislative body is elected entirely through a proportional representation system based on party lists.

The new unicameral Parliament, called the Kurultai, was established earlier this year following constitutional reforms promoted by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. It replaced Kazakhstan’s former two-chamber parliament, abolishing the upper house and the mixed electoral system under which voters could also choose candidates directly, rather than only from party lists.

title: Europol Warns of Violent Shift in European Museum Heists
content:
Europol is warning of an alarming shift in museum heists across Europe, as criminal networks abandon traditional stealth in favor of brute force and extreme violence, according to a report published Monday.

The European Union’s law enforcement agency said perpetrators are increasingly ditching the traditional “deception and discreet execution” of art theft, historically viewed as a “non-violent form of organized property crime,” in favor of direct and confrontational methods.

Instead of niche experts, Europol’s report—”Changing Tactics, Changing Targets: The Evolving Nature of Museum Heists”—found that these new heists are often carried out by decentralized groups of opportunistic criminals recruited via social media on a “crime-as-a-service” basis. These new criminal profiles are increasingly armed with sledgehammers, axes, crowbars, and explosives and firearms to breach premises, smash display cases and intimidate or assault staff in broad daylight.

title: Philippines Arrests South Korean Woman Over Alleged $3.9B Online Gambling Operation
content:
Philippine immigration authorities have arrested a 29-year-old South Korean woman wanted in her home country for allegedly helping operate 23 illegal online gambling websites that generated about 5.33 trillion won ($3.9 billion), the country’s Bureau of Immigration said.

Kim Youngsun was detained on August 7 in General Trias, Cavite, in an operation coordinated with South Korean authorities and the Philippine National Police. The Incheon District Court issued a warrant for her arrest in April 2025, and Interpol published a Red Notice two months later. Authorities allege that Kim worked as an assistant manager and supervised several units of the gambling operation, which was run from offices in Pasay and Quezon City beginning in 2018. She is being held at the Bureau of Immigration’s Warden Facility pending custodial proceedings.

OCCRP asked the Philippine Bureau of Immigration to forward a request for comment to Kim but had not received a response by the time of publication.

title: Moscow Funds Pro-Kremlin Influence Hub in Belarus
content:
A Moscow-funded cultural center in Minsk has operated as an ideological influence hub for the Kremlin, using hundreds of thousands of dollars in Russian state funds to promote the “Russian world” ideology and cement Moscow’s grip over Belarus, according to leaked internal documents.

The cache of more than 270,000 emails from the Moscow House of Compatriots - obtained by Danish public broadcaster DR and analyzed by OCCRP’s Belarusian member center Buro Media - reveals the scale of Russia’s soft-power spending in its neighbor’s capital.

The House of Moscow in Minsk is the Belarusian branch of the Moscow House of Compatriots, a Russian state organization that works with Russian-speaking communities abroad. Although conceived as a business bridge between Moscow and Minsk, it instead hosted events promoting Russian language, joint historical identity, and Kremlin geopolitical priorities.

These efforts mirror Russia’s so-called “humanitarian policy abroad” - a foreign policy doctrine approved by President Vladimir V. Putin that emphasizes defending the ideals of Russkiy Mir, or the “Russian world,” and countering what Moscow labels “Russophobia.”

title: Liberia Charges Ex-Vice President in Transnational Drug Probe
content:
Liberian prosecutors have charged former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor with drug trafficking, money laundering, and other offenses in connection with an investigation into an alleged transnational narcotics network, the country’s authorities announced late Wednesday.

Howard-Taylor, who served as vice president from 2018 to 2024, was arrested on August 19, 2026, at Roberts International Airport and taken to the headquarters of the Liberia National Police, according to a statement from the Ministry of Information.

In a separate Facebook statement, the Information Ministry confirmed that the charges stem from a record $317 million drug bust on July 21, 2026, when officers seized nearly four metric tons of cocaine in Duazon, east of the capital Monrovia. Two foreign nationals were arrested during the operation, which authorities described as the one of the largest narcotics bust in the country's history: one holding dual Spanish and Colombian passports and the other a Serbian passport.

title: Zelenskyy Dismisses Senior Aide Suspected in $3.3 Million Money Laundering Case
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy dismissed senior aide Iryna Mudra on the same day she said anti-corruption investigators had notified her of suspicion in a case involving the alleged laundering of 150 million hryvnias ($3.3 million).

Zelenskyy removed Mudra as deputy head of the Presidential Office without giving a reason for the move.

Ukraine’s National Anti-Corruption Bureau (NABU) and Specialized Anti-Corruption Prosecutor’s Office said in an official ⁠video that their operation, codenamed “Forest Gump,” had uncovered a group that allegedly laundered criminal proceeds through the formal financial system.

According to investigators, the group included a deputy head of the Ukrainian Presidential Office, a former member of parliament, the chair of the management board of a state-owned bank, the chair of its supervisory board and others. The authorities did not identify them by name in the video.

The 150 million hryvnias in cash was allegedly moved through accounts belonging to shell companies and then used to post bail for an alleged member of a criminal organization investigated in the separate “Midas” corruption case. The video did not identify the person whose bail was paid.

title: French Authorities Investigate Widespread Government Data Breaches
content:
French authorities are investigating a series of major cyberattacks after a hack of the Ministry of Public Action and Accounts compromised the personal and financial data of nearly 700,000 individuals and businesses. The stolen records—which include taxable income, family quotient data, withholding tax rates, land registry records, and probate files—came to light after being put up for sale on a hacking forum.

The French National Police’s anticybercrime unit is leading the investigation into the breach. The incident follows a separate late-July cyberattack targeting the Ministry of National Education, with media reports indicating that the same hacker claimed responsibility for selling data extracted from both government systems.

Additionally, ministry officials disclosed that hackers compromised Bloctel, an official government service that allowed users to block telemarketing calls before shutting down on August 11. That breach exposed files containing 3 million phone numbers.

title: Interrogation Tapes Reveal Journalist Murder Suspect Pointing to Highest Levels of Maltese Power
content:
Audio recordings of police interrogations played to a Maltese jury this week revealed that Yorgen Fenech, the businessman on trial for the 2017 car bomb assassination of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia, pointed the finger at the highest levels of government at the time, claiming the murder was commissioned by the former prime minister’s chief of staff.

Caruana Galizia, 53, who spent years reporting on corruption at the top of the Maltese state, was killed by a car bomb in October 2017. 

In police interviews recorded in November 2019, he told investigators that Keith Schembri, then chief of staff to Prime Minister Joseph Muscat, had pressed him for years to arrange the murder. Fenech said that the more than 450,000 euros he subsequently paid to the confessed middleman Melvin Theuma was not a murder fee, but money extorted from him through blackmail.

"Everything started with Keith Schembri," Fenech told Superintendent Kurt Zahra during the interrogation. "I was commissioned by Keith Schembri. He was pushing for this murder. I was never the one who sent anyone or did anything."

title: US Charges Eight More Iranians in Global Hacking Case
content:
U.S. prosecutors have charged eight additional Iranians in an alleged state-linked hacking campaign that targeted universities, companies and government agencies worldwide. The expanded indictment brings the number of defendants linked to the Tehran-based Mabna Institute to 17, nine of whom were originally charged in 2018. Prosecutors allege the institute carried out attacks for Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and other Iranian clients.

The hackers allegedly targeted more than 100,000 academic accounts and compromised around 8,000 of them at 322 universities, stealing at least 31.5 terabytes of research and intellectual property, the U.S. Justice Department said. They also allegedly breached companies, U.S. government agencies, the United Nations and UNICEF, and sold stolen academic materials through Iranian websites. The U.S. State Department is offering rewards of up to $10 million for information leading to the location of five of the defendants.

title: Indonesia Seizes Record 2.6 Tons of Meth in Major Bust, 10 Arrested
content:
Indonesian authorities have seized 2.6 metric tons of liquid methamphetamine hidden aboard a Tanzanian-flagged vessel in one of the country’s largest drug busts, the National Narcotics Agency announced Tuesday, according to state news agency Antara.

Officers discovered the liquid methamphetamine stored in eight water barrels and inside the water tank of the MV Ocean Porter. Authorities also found a 40-foot container holding 157 boxes of illegal cigarettes on board. Ten crew members, all Myanmar nationals, were arrested.

The operation marks the second major drug intercept involving a Tanzanian-flagged vessel this month, following the confiscation of nearly 1.3 metric tons of ketamine in a separate operation.

title: Iran Moves to Outlaw All Contact With "Hostile" Foreign Media
content:
Iran’s parliament has approved the general framework of a bill that would criminalize speaking to or sharing data with foreign media outlets deemed "hostile." Human rights groups warned that the move is a dangerous attempt to isolate the country from the outside world and hide evidence of internal dissent.

The preliminary vote advances legislation that would prohibit citizens from giving interviews, communicating, or sharing information with external news organizations, particularly those affiliated with the United States or Israel. Under the draft bill, violators face between six months and two years in prison, RFE/RL’s Persian section, Radio Farda, reported. 

Iranian officials framed the proposed law as a vital national security measure. Abbas Goudarzi, a spokesman for the parliamentary presidium, told state media that any communications that “facilitate foreign influence” over Iran would be outlawed under the new statute.

To become law, the bill's specific provisions must be debated by lawmakers and in the end approved by the Guardian Council, a 12-member body of clerics and jurists responsible for vetting all legislation for compliance with Islamic law and the Iranian constitution.

title: A Key Food Source Collapsed Off West Africa’s Coast as Chinese Ships Ground the Species Into Fishmeal
content:
As the day draws to a close in Bubaque, a remote island in Guinea-Bissau, fishermen are arriving with their day’s catch, pulling canoes onto a muddy bank teeming with crabs.

It’s a common scene here in the Bijagós Archipelago, and elsewhere along the West African coast. And one species is especially prized as a source of high-quality protein — the sardinella.

But the small and silvery fish has been decimated in Guinea-Bissau’s coastal waters, according to an internal fisheries assessment produced for the government and obtained by OCCRP.

The assessment was carried out in 2025 by the Atlantic branch of the Russian Federal Research Institute of Fisheries and Oceanography (VNIRO), which worked with scientists from INIPO, Guinea-Bissau’s oceanographic institute. 

While the assessment does not delve into the cause of the decline, a government official attributed it to the recent rise of the local fishmeal industry, which grinds up large volumes of the sardinella and other fish to make a nutrient-dense powder that is fed to farm animals around the world.

title: US Unseals 25-Count Indictment in $165M Crypto Case
content:
Federal prosecutors in Georgia have unsealed a 25-count indictment against an American man accused of orchestrating a $165 million cryptocurrency Ponzi scheme that defrauded thousands of investors, just days after authorities in Fiji apprehended him and handed him over to federal agents.

The indictment, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Georgia, marks the culmination of an international hunt for Edward Zimbardi, 59, who prosecutors say promised up to 25 percent monthly returns through high-yield investment platforms before fleeing to the South Pacific as federal regulators closed in.

Zimbardi was scheduled to appear in federal court in Los Angeles on Monday on 12 counts of wire fraud, 12 counts of money laundering, and one count of money laundering conspiracy. He did not respond to an earlier request for comment.

“Zimbardi allegedly tricked thousands of people into investing in his ‘Crypto Program’ with false promises of enormous returns. Instead, he spent the money on risky currency trades, payments to early investors, and treating himself to a house and expensive vehicles,” U.S. Attorney Theodore S. Hertzberg said in a statement.

title: Fiji Hands Over a Man Suspected of Ponzi-style Crypto Investment Schemes to US
content:
Fiji handed over an American citizen suspected of involvement in multi-million-dollar cryptocurrency Ponzi schemes across the United States that promised participants returns as high as 25 percent a month and encouraged them to recruit friends and acquaintances for bonuses.

The suspect, Edward Zimbardi, 59, was “removed” from Fiji and returned to the United States last week as part of a joint operation by the FBI and Fiji’s Ministry of Immigration, senior Fiji immigration officials told OCCRP.

Zimbardi did not respond to a request for comment, and it was not immediately clear if he had been formally charged in the United States. The U.S. embassy referred questions to the FBI and the U.S. Department of Justice, and Fijian immigration officials said an FBI announcement was expected in the coming days.

Zimbardi’s legal troubles began in 1997 when he was convicted in Georgia of felony theft and served roughly 17 months in prison.

title: Iraqi Electricity Official Arrested With Millions in Cash as Anti-Graft Campaign Expands
content:
In what appears to be the latest escalation of a sweeping anti-corruption campaign launched by Iraq’s new prime minister, Ali al-Zaidi, federal authorities have arrested the undersecretary of the Ministry of Electricity, seizing millions of dollars in cash and gold bars from his properties.

The official, Khalid Ghazay Atiya, was arrested on Aug. 14 by the Federal Commission of Integrity on charges of corruption and illicit enrichment, according to the country’s official Iraqi News Agency.

Investigators executed search warrants at Atiya's residences, uncovering $5.839 million and 1.175 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $900,000) in cash, alongside seven gold bars and alloys. The commission submitted the seized assets to an investigating judge for further legal action.

title: Spain Seizes 13 Tonnes of Nitrous Oxide in Tenerife
content:
Spain’s Civil Guard dismantled an alleged criminal organization accused of illegally importing and distributing nitrous oxide, commonly known as laughing gas, in Tenerife, seizing nearly 13 tons of the substance in what authorities called Europe’s second-largest haul.

Six people were arrested and another six placed under investigation for alleged involvement in a criminal organization, drug trafficking, trafficking in substances harmful to health, and money laundering, the Civil Guard said. During searches in Arona, Adeje and Granadilla de Abona, officers seized 10,394 containers holding almost 13,000 kilograms of nitrous oxide, as well as 63,500 euros (US$74,000) and 1,000 pounds (US$1,350) in cash.

Authorities also confiscated cocaine, hashish, marijuana and “tusi,” along with imitation firearms and bladed weapons. Investigators said the alleged organization was headed by members of one family and divided into branches responsible for importing the gas from abroad, storing it in properties around the island, and distributing it to customers. The investigation remains ongoing and further arrests are possible, according to the Civil Guard.
